url: /mimus/tutorials/first-run.md
---
# Tutorial: your first check

Goal: verify a repo's documented claims in minutes.

## 1. Init

```sh
cd your-repo
mimus init
```

Detects claim sources (README, docs/, AGENTS.md, code comments,
`.kuda/` cards) and writes `mimus.toml` + a `rules/` dir.

## 2. Check the mechanical tier

```sh
mimus check
```

Extracts claims and verifies what can be proven:

* `path` — referenced files/dirs exist
* `command` — documented commands parse and exit clean
* `symbol` — names resolve (via the kuda index when present)
* `count` — asserted numbers recompute ("357 suites…")
* `link` — URLs resolve

Output is CI-gateable: violations only, each with claim +
evidence + fix.

## 3. Report

```sh
mimus report          # everything found, grouped by source
mimus check --all     # + semantic tier (advisory, never gates)
```

## 4. Wire into CI

```sh
mimus check --format json   # machine-readable for gates
```

Docs become tested artifacts — a claim that breaks fails the
build like a failing test.

# How-to: watch multiple repos

Add one `[[repo]]` entry per repository; `name` must equal the
payload's `repository.full_name`. Each repo gets its own pending
slot; a single global worker serializes runs (deliberate — safe on
one box). Same-repo pushes may cancel their own in-flight run
(`cancel_running`); a push never cancels another repo's run.

```toml
[[repo]]
name = "org/api"
dir = "/srv/checkouts/api"
queue = "all" # every push runs (releases)

[[repo]]
name = "org/web"
dir = "/srv/checkouts/web" # default latest-wins

# [repo.runner]                # per-repo override; replaces global
#   kind = "shell"
#   cmd = "./release.sh"
```

Run `mimus deploy webhook` once — it registers the hook on every
watched repo. `status_repo` on an entry redirects statuses (e.g.
mirror repos); it defaults to `name`.

url: /mimus/how-to/kuda-audit.md

# How-to: audit the memory layer

`mimus audit` applies the same claim machinery to `.kuda/`
cards — agent memory gets a trust score, not a free pass.

## Run

```sh
mimus audit
```

Per card it verifies:

* every `verify:` file still exists
* card `provenance.files` hashes match current content
* symbols claimed in `api:` resolve in the index
* `deps:` edges match the real dep graph

## Reading the score

Each card reports `trust`: fresh | drifted | contradicted.
Drifted cards should be regenerated (`kuda sync`); contradicted
cards need attention — either the code moved without a sync, or
the summarizer invented something (a bug worth reporting).

## Why it matters

Memory without falsification decays into confident confabulation.
The audit is what makes a kuda index *trustworthy* rather than
merely *present*.

# How-to: author convention rules

Conventions live as data in `rules/*.toml` — never in engine
code. A new rule is a file, not a release.

## A rule

```toml
# rules/no-kind-dispatch.toml
name = "no-kind-dispatch"
message = "dispatch via lang.child_role_index — kind == is a regression"
severity = "error"
match = { kind = "source-pattern", pattern = 'kind == "(assign|block|paren)"' }
files = "crates/**/src/*.rs"
```

Rule kinds:

* `source-pattern` — regex over source files
* `doc-claim` — a prose claim that must verify (e.g. "README's
  build command exits clean")
* `structure` — graph assertions ("engine crates never depend
  on cli")

## Semantics

* `severity = "error"` fails `mimus check`; `"warn"` only
  appears in `report`.
* Keep rules mechanically checkable — if a rule can't carry
  evidence, it doesn't belong here (see ADR-0001).
* Rules are per-repo — convention packs for ecosystems are a
  backlog item.

# Command-Line Help for `mimus`

This document contains the help content for the `mimus` command-line program.

**Command Overview:**

* [`mimus`↴](#mimus)
* [`mimus init`↴](#mimus-init)
* [`mimus check`↴](#mimus-check)
* [`mimus audit`↴](#mimus-audit)
* [`mimus report`↴](#mimus-report)
* [`mimus doctor`↴](#mimus-doctor)

## `mimus`

Spots the cuckoo eggs in your repo — claim verification: docs-as-tests, memory audit

**Usage:** `mimus [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `init` — Detect sources -> mimus.toml + rules/ scaffold
* `check` — Verify claims. Mechanical tier by default
* `audit` — Trust-score .kuda/ cards vs source
* `report` — Full violations list with evidence
* `doctor` — Checker/config/kuda-index health

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (else $MIMUS_CONFIG, ./mimus.toml, ~/.config/mimus/mimus.toml)
* `--format <FORMAT>` — Output format: human | json

  Default value: `human`

## `mimus init`

Detect sources -> mimus.toml + rules/ scaffold

**Usage:** `mimus init`

## `mimus check`

Verify claims. Mechanical tier by default

**Usage:** `mimus check [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--all` — Include the semantic tier (advisory only, never gates)
* `--no-cmd` — Never execute documented commands

## `mimus audit`

Trust-score .kuda/ cards vs source

**Usage:** `mimus audit`

## `mimus report`

Full violations list with evidence

**Usage:** `mimus report`

## `mimus doctor`

Checker/config/kuda-index health

**Usage:** `mimus doctor`

&#xA;This document was generated automatically by
clap-markdown.&#xA;

# Config — `mimus.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sources` | `SourcesCfg` | optional | — |
| `check` | `CheckCfg` | optional | — |
| `rules` | `RulesCfg` | optional | — |
| `report` | `ReportCfg` | optional | — |

## `[sources]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs` | `list` | optional | Doc glob patterns mined for claims. |
| `comments` | `bool` | optional | Extract claims from code comments too. |
| `cards` | `string` | optional | Glob for memory cards to audit (empty = skip). |

## `[check]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mechanical` | `bool` | optional | Mechanical tier — deterministic, CI-gateable. |
| `semantic` | `bool` | optional | Semantic tier — advisory only, can never gate. |
| `kuda_index` | `path` | optional | kuda index path for the symbol checker. |

## `[rules]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `path` | optional | Dir of \*.toml rule files. |
| `strict` | `bool` | optional | Rule violations also fail `check` (not just report). |

## `[report]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | `string` | optional | "human" | "json". |
| `min_confidence` | `string` | optional | Suppress low-evidence findings ("high" | "all"). |

## Constraints

* `queue = "all"` rejects `cancel_running = true` at load —
  killing a run would silently drop a promised commit.
* `runner.kind` and `trigger.kind`/`status.kind` resolve to impl
  crates; unknown kinds fail at `mimus doctor`/startup.
* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.

# Explanation: architecture

## Claims, not opinions

Docs and memory cards make *claims*: this path exists, this
command works, this symbol lives here, this number is current.
mimus extracts claims into a taxonomy — each type routes to the
checker that can actually prove or refute it:

| claim      | checker                | tier       |
| ---------- | ---------------------- | ---------- |
| `path`     | `check-fs`             | mechanical |
| `command`  | `check-cmd`            | mechanical |
| `symbol`   | `check-symbol` (kuda)  | mechanical |
| `count`    | `check-cmd`/`check-fs` | mechanical |
| `link`     | `check-link` (planned) | mechanical |
| `behavior` | `check-llm` (planned)  | semantic   |

## The evidence bar

A violation is claim + evidence + suggested fix. No evidence, no
finding — false positives kill a critic faster than false
negatives. The semantic tier can never gate CI: it reports, a
human adjudicates. Style opinions are never emitted at all.

## Ports and adapters

Every concern is a trait crate + adapter crates: checkers
(`fs` | `cmd` | `symbol` | `llm`), claim sources (md, comments,
cards), sinks (cli, commit-status). Rules are data
(`rules/*.toml`) — conventions as files, not code.

## Position in the ecosystem

* `kuda` builds the index; `mimus` doubts it — `audit`
  trust-scores cards against source via the `symbol` checker.
* `reconcile` (planned third tool) auto-fixes what mimus
  confirms: claims rewritten to match reality.

---

---
url: /mimus/explanation/release-model.md
---
# The release model

mimus releases itself — there is no hosted CI and no release tool
in the loop. Two deliberate phases:

## Phase 1 — the explicit seed

`mimus deploy release` runs once, by hand: it reads cargo metadata,
topologically orders the workspace's path-dependency graph,
`cargo publish`es every member, tags `{repo}-v{version}`, and pushes
the tag.

Why explicit? Publishing is the **only irreversible step** in the
whole system. Queues, runs, and statuses are all idempotent and
local; a crate version on crates.io is forever. Everything else in
mimus fires on push — the seed doesn't. (`--dry-run` prints the
order and tag without touching anything.)

## Phase 2 — push-driven forever after

From then on a release is *just another mimus job*: a push to `main`
hits the webhook, queues latest-wins, and runs `scripts/release.sh`
in a detached worktree under the shell runner.

The script:

1. diffs crate paths since the last `mimus-v*` tag
2. `cargo set-version --bump patch` on touched crates only (the cli
   republishes on any change — it's the install artifact)
3. `cargo publish`es them in dep order
4. tags `mimus-vX.Y.Z`, builds host-arch binaries with `cargo dist`,
   uploads to a GitHub Release via `gh`

The 5-minute sleep at the top isn't a hack — it's the debounce
window. Combined with `queue = "latest"` + `cancel_running`, rapid
push bursts collapse to one release of the newest sha; killed runs
get an honest "cancelled" status.

## Why this shape

* **No release-plz / GHA**: the point of the project is that CI is a
  local loop — depending on hosted CI to ship it would be
  self-defeating. `release.sh` is deliberately boring bash so it can
  run as a plain `cmd` under `runner.kind = "shell"`.
* **Latest-wins, not `all`**: a release that misses an intermediate
  push loses nothing — the tag lands on HEAD, which contains
  everything. `queue = "all"` is for pipelines where each sha's run
  is individually meaningful.
* **Explicit over automatic**: a wrong tag or half-published
  workspace is far worse than a delayed release; the boundary sits
  exactly at irreversibility.

Host prerequisites: `cargo-edit`, `cargo-dist`, `gh`, and
`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (env → keyring → env file). Multi-arch
binaries arrive when the remote-runner pair lands — see TODO.

# mimus vs the alternatives

## vs linters

|                     | linters              | mimus                       |
| ------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| checks              | code shape           | claims about reality          |
| docs                | mostly ignored       | first-class source            |
| output              | style/correctness    | claim + evidence + fix        |
| rules               | per-language config  | `rules/*.toml`, evidence-bound|

They complement each other — a linter says the code is shaped
right; mimus says the docs tell the truth.

## vs LLM doc review

|                     | "review the docs" prompt | mimus                    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------- |
| coverage            | broad, vague             | only what's checkable      |
| false positives     | high                     | evidence-or-silence        |
| CI gate             | unsafe                   | mechanical tier is safe    |
| cost                | per-run                  | mechanical tier is free    |

The LLM still has a role — as the `check-llm` adapter for the
semantic tier, where findings are advisory by design.

## vs doctest-style tools

|                     | doctests/link-checkers | mimus                       |
| ------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| scope               | code blocks only       | all factual prose             |
| claim types         | one or two             | path/cmd/symbol/count/link    |
| memory audit        | n/a                    | `.kuda/` card trust scores    |

# Getting started

Pick by what you need to do.

* **Tutorials** (learn): [first-run](tutorials/first-run.md)
* **How-to** (tasks): [memory audit](how-to/kuda-audit.md) ·
  [rules authoring](how-to/rules-authoring.md)
* **Reference** (lookup): [cli](reference/cli.md) ·
  [config](reference/config.md) ·
  [crate api](reference/crate-api.md)
* **Explanation** (why): [architecture](explanation/architecture.md) ·
  [release model](explanation/release-model.md) ·
  [comparison](comparison.md) — vs linters / LLM review

Install:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/mimus mimus
```

First check:

```sh
cd your-repo
mimus init    # detect claim sources -> mimus.toml + rules/
mimus check   # mechanical tier: paths, commands, symbols
mimus report  # violations with claim + evidence + fix
```
